acme_cust: Hi team — starting ~09:12 UTC today our app saw ~400-900ms latency spikes for text-generation calls. Customer insists they set region=eu-central-1 in the SDK but traces show convo hitting us-west-2. Trace id 3b9f2a9e. Help please.

jai_support: sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a sample request id / trace? any auth errors?

acme_cust: no auth errors, requests succeed but slow. sample req_id: r-20260317-3b9f2a9e, reproducible from their EU-based clients.

jai_support: thx. tagging infra @sarah_ops @mike_infra to run a tracewalk and check routing tables + gateway fallbacks. :eyes:

sarah_ops: grabbing traces now. from the payload we see the header X-Redwood-Region: eu-central-1, payload size ~3.2k tokens. SDK shows region preference set.

mike_infra: ran a quick trace on r-20260317-3b9f2a9e, attached hop summary below:
```
client (eu) -> edge-eu-2 -> gw-eu -> api-gateway-global -> cluster-usw2 -> model-worker-usw2
latency: 120ms -> 15ms -> 10ms -> 260ms -> 420ms
```
This looks like gateway-global is failing over to a US cluster.

laura_prod: is this a capacity fallback or a routing policy issue? we have a policy that allows global fallback when eu capacity < 2x requests. any recent canaries?

sarah_ops: checked capacity: eu clusters are healthy and under 60% CPU. no autoscale events. gateway-global logs show a 504 on a cached routing entry which caused a lookup to fallback to default-route which points to region priority [us-west-2,...] due to a stale cache entry.

mike_infra: reproducer command from our side (curl):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-central-1" -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate
```
When routed through our global gateway we see the response header `x-redwood-routed-region: us-west-2`.

jai_support: can we surface the routed-region in the SDK so customer sees it in logs? also need a mitigation ASAP — sticky region routing or deny global fallback for tenant acme-123 until fix deployed.

sarah_ops: adding a temporary routing rule: tenant=acme-123 enforce_region=eu-central-1 at gateway layer. rolling in 2m. will monitor p99.

netbot: incident created: INC-2026-0341 assigned to mike_infra. Pager sent to infra oncall.

mike_infra: root cause summary: cache miss on gateway-global routing table + fallback rule that defaults to global priority list. staleness window was 5m due to new rollout bug. fix: patch gateway cache invalidation to respect route TTL and add tenant-level affinity override. patch rolling now.

laura_prod: action items: 1) keep tenant override until next deploy; 2) add SDK header echo `x-redwood-routed-region` in debug builds; 3) add alert when gateway routes >5% traffic outside requested region for any tenant. filing tickets.

acme_cust: thanks team. can you confirm when the sticky rule is in effect? customers still seeing occasional spikes.

sarah_ops: sticky rule live at 09:29 UTC. can you run a quick repro? if you still see us-west-2 provide new req_id.

acme_cust: running now, will report back in 10m. thanks. :thumbsup:

mike_infra: post-mortem note: root cause tied to rollout 20260316-rtg-v2 where TTL config defaulted to 300s instead of honoring service-provided 30s. short-term mitigation applied. longer-term: add integration tests for route TTL and tenant affinity.

laura_prod: assigning follow-ups: RD-1123 (gateway TTL fix) -> mike_infra, RD-1124 (SDK echo header) -> devex, RD-1125 (routing alert) -> observability.

acme_cust: rechecked at 09:40 UTC — p99 reduced back to baseline. will reopen if we see more. thank you all.

jai_support: closing loop here; please reopen with req_id if it recurs. :white_check_mark:
